intent: Baseline symmetric five-sensor array ahead of the axle with weights proportional to sensor lateral position, so the steering signal is a clean, correctly signed lateral error. Geometry is mid-range to give the Integrator a stable starting platform. The purpose is to get a first race and integration feedback before changing the array.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Next iteration, check whether the sensor spacing gives a usable signal on the sharpest bends (does the signal saturate or drop out?) and whether line-loss events occur at the bend entries, which would point to the sensor lookahead y or the array width.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no Integrator feedback yet, so this is a baseline design built from the contract alone. Five sensors span x = -0.02 to +0.02 m at 0.01 m spacing, all 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so they read the line slightly ahead of the wheels. The 0.012 m footprint is a little smaller than the 25 mm tape, so one sensor can sit fully on the tape while the outer ones still see an edge. Weights are set proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal is a direct, sign-correct lateral error: a line to the left gives a positive signal and steers left, as the contract requires. Wheel track 0.12 m and body width 0.12 m keep the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor, which gives a comfortable margin. A 0.03 m wheel radius and 0.8 kg mass sit in the middle of their ranges, keeping yaw inertia moderate so the robot can turn on the tighter bends without excessive overshoot. I expect a run that completes the oval with a modest rms_error, with the main risk being speed limits on the slalom.
